questions.question: A sum of money becomes Rs. 6,400 in 3 years and Rs. 8,100 in 5 years on compound interest compounded annually. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money becomes Rs. 6,400 in 3 years and Rs. 8,100 in 5 years on compound interest compounded annually. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount after 3 years = Rs. 6,400.

Amount after 5 years = Rs. 8,100.

Formula Used:

Amount = Principal × (1 + Rate/100)Time

Compound Interest for n years = Amount - Principal

Calculation:

Let the principal be P and the rate be R% per annum.

⇒ P × (1 + R/100)3 = 6,400

⇒ P × (1 + R/100)5 = 8,100

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get:

⇒ (1 + R/100)5 / (1 + R/100)3 = 8,100 / 6,400

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = 8,100 / 6,400

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = 81/64

⇒ 1 + R/100 = √(81/64)

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 9/8

⇒ R/100 = 1/8

⇒ R = 12.5%

⇒ R = 12 (4/8) %

The rate of interest per annum is 12 (4/8) %.

questions.question: A chair is sold for Rs. 720 after giving a discount of 10% on its marked price. The cost price of the chair is Rs. 640. If it is sold at the marked price, then the profit percentage will be:
questions.questionHtml: A chair is sold for Rs. 720 after giving a discount of 10% on its marked price. The cost price of the chair is Rs. 640. If it is sold at the marked price, then the profit percentage will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling price of the chair = Rs. 720

Discount % = 10

Cost price of the chair = Rs. 640

Concept used:

Selling price = Marked price - Marked price × discount%

Profit = Selling price - cost price

Profit % = (profit/cost price) × 100

Calculation:

Let the marked price of the article be 10a

According to the question,

10a - 10a × 10% = 720

⇒ 9a = 720

⇒ a = 720/9 = 80

So, the marked price of the chair = 10 × 80

⇒ Rs. 800

Now,

Profit on the chair when it is sold at marked price = 800 - 640

⇒ Rs. 160

Profit % = (160/640) × 100

⇒ 25

∴ The profit percentage will be 25%.

questions.question: In a mixture of 60 litres, the ratio of milk to water is 2 : 3. If this ratio is required to be 7 : 9 then the quantity of Milk to be added further will be-
questions.questionHtml: In a mixture of 60 litres, the ratio of milk to water is 2 : 3. If this ratio is required to be 7 : 9 then the quantity of Milk to be added further will be-
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial Milk : Water = 2 : 3. To keep water constant for the 7 : 9 target, multiply initial ratio by 3.

New Initial Ratio = (2 × 3) : (3 × 3) = 6 : 9. Final Ratio = 7 : 9.

Initial total parts = 6 + 9 = 15 units. Given 15 units = 60 L ⇒ 1 unit = 4 L.

Increase in Milk = 7 − 6 = 1 unit.

Added Milk = 1 × 4 L = 4 L.

∴ The correct answer is 4 L.

Alternate Method

Given: Total Mixture = 60 L, Initial Ratio (Milk : Water) = 2 : 3.

Formula: Quantity = [Ratio Part ÷ Total Parts] × Total Quantity

⇒ Initial Milk = (2 / 5) × 60 = 24 L

⇒ Initial Water = (3 / 5) × 60 = 36 L

⇒ Let the quantity of Milk added be 'x' L.

⇒ New Milk = 24 + x

⇒ New Ratio = (24 + x) / 36 = 7 / 9

⇒ 9 × (24 + x) = 7 × 36

⇒ 216 + 9x = 252

⇒ 9x = 252 − 216 = 36

⇒ x = 36 ÷ 9 = 4 L

∴ The correct answer is 4 L.

Additional Information

Constant Quantity Rule

When only one component is added to a mixture, the quantity of the other component remains constant. Equating the constant parts in ratios simplifies calculations.

Ratio and Proportion

If a : b is the ratio, then total parts = a + b. Each part's value = (Total Quantity) ÷ (a + b).

Replacement vs. Addition

In addition, the total volume increases. In replacement, some mixture is removed and replaced by a component, keeping total volume constant.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells a cricket bat whose marked price is Rs. 30, at a discount of 15%, and gives a ball costing Rs. 1.50 free with each bat. Even then he makes a profit of 20%. his cost price, per bat is:
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper sells a cricket bat whose marked price is Rs. 30, at a discount of 15%, and gives a ball costing Rs. 1.50 free with each bat. Even then he makes a profit of 20%. his cost price, per bat is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net Revenue (Effective SP) = (85% of 30) − Cost of free item

Effective SP = 25.50 − 1.50 = Rs. 24

Profit = 20% ⇒ CP = Effective SP ÷ 1.2

CP = 24 ÷ 1.2 = Rs. 20

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 20.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marked Price (MP) of the bat = Rs. 30

Discount = 15%

Cost of free ball = Rs. 1.50

Profit percentage = 20%

Calculations:

⇒ Discount amount on bat = 15% of 30 = (15 ÷ 100) × 30 = Rs. 4.50

⇒ Amount collected from customer = 30 − 4.50 = Rs. 25.50

⇒ Effective Selling Price (SP) = Amount collected − Cost of free item

⇒ Effective SP = 25.50 − 1.50 = Rs. 24.00

⇒ Profit = 20% on CP

⇒ CP × (1 + 20 ÷ 100) = 24

⇒ CP × 1.2 = 24

⇒ CP = 24 ÷ 1.2 = Rs. 20

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 20.

Additional Information

Relationship between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This formula is used when no extra free items are given.

Effective Selling Price

When a free item is given, the cost of that item must be subtracted from the actual SP to find the net revenue earned by the seller.

Basic Profit Formula

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: A sector of pizza is cut from the circular pizza of radius 21 cm, the angle of the sector being 120°. If another pizza of the same area as the sector of pizza is formed, then the diameter (in cm) of the new pizza is:
questions.questionHtml: A sector of pizza is cut from the circular pizza of radius 21 cm, the angle of the sector being 120°. If another pizza of the same area as the sector of pizza is formed, then the diameter (in cm) of the new pizza is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of sector = Area of new pizza

(120°/360°) × π × (21)2 = π × R2

(1/3) × 21 × 21 = R2 ⇒ R2 = 7 × 21 = 147

R = √147 = 7√3 cm

Diameter = 2R = 14√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 14√3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of original pizza (r) = 21 cm

Angle of sector (θ) = 120°

Formula Used:

Area of sector = (θ/360°) × πr2

Area of circle = πR2

Calculations:

⇒ Area of sector = (120/360) × π × 21 × 21

⇒ Area of sector = (1/3) × π × 441 = 147π cm2

⇒ Let R be the radius of the new pizza.

⇒ πR2 = 147π

⇒ R2 = 147

⇒ R = √(49 × 3) = 7√3 cm

⇒ Diameter of new pizza = 2 × R = 2 × 7√3

⇒ Diameter = 14√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 14√3 cm.

Additional Information

Area and Perimeter of a Sector

The length of an arc is (L) = (θ/360°) × 2πr and the perimeter of a sector is L + 2r.

Relation between Area and Arc Length

Area of a sector can also be calculated as (1/2) × L × r, where L is the arc length.

Circle Properties

Diameter is the longest chord of a circle and is equal to twice the radius (D = 2r).

questions.question: A man sold two watches, each for Rs. 495. If he gained 10% on one watch and suffered a loss of 10% on the other, then what is the loss or gain percentage in the transaction?
questions.questionHtml: A man sold two watches, each for Rs. 495. If he gained 10% on one watch and suffered a loss of 10% on the other, then what is the loss or gain percentage in the transaction?
questions.solution:
C.P. of first article = (495 × 100) / (100 + 10) = 49500 / 110 = Rs. 450

C.P. of second article = (495 × 100) / (100 - 10) = 49500 / 90 = Rs. 550

Total C.P. = 450 + 550 = Rs. 1000

Total S.P. = 495 + 495 = Rs. 990

Loss% = ((1000 - 990) / 1000) × 100 = 1%

questions.question: The slant height and radius of a right circular cone are in the ratio 29 ∶ 20. If its volume is 4838.4 π cm 3 , then its radius is:
questions.questionHtml: The slant height and radius of a right circular cone are in the ratio 29 ∶ 20. If its volume is 4838.4 π cm<sup>3</sup>, then its radius is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given ratio of Slant height (l) : Radius (r) = 29 : 20.

Using Pythagorean triplet (20, 21, 29), the height (h) corresponds to 21 parts.

Volume part = 1/3 × r2 × h = 1/3 × 202 × 21 = 2800 units3.

Comparing with actual volume: x3 = 4838.4 / 2800 = 1.728 ⇒ x = 1.2.

Radius (r) = 20 × 1.2 = 24 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of l : r = 29 : 20

Volume of cone (V) = 4838.4 π cm3

Formula:

Volume of cone = (1/3) π r2 h

Relation between l, r, and h: l2 = r2 + h2

Let common ratio be x. Then r = 20x and l = 29x.

⇒ h = √(l2 − r2) = √((29x)2 − (20x)2)

⇒ h = √(841x2 − 400x2) = √(441x2) = 21x

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × (20x)2 × (21x) = 4838.4 π

⇒ (1/3) × 400x2 × 21x = 4838.4

⇒ 400 × 7x3 = 4838.4

⇒ 2800x3 = 4838.4

⇒ x3 = 4838.4 ÷ 2800 = 1.728

⇒ x = ³√1.728 = 1.2

⇒ Radius (r) = 20x = 20 × 1.2 = 24 cm

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Additional Information

Curved Surface Area of Cone

The lateral surface area or CSA of a right circular cone is given by the formula CSA = πrl, where r is radius and l is slant height.

Total Surface Area of Cone

The TSA includes the base area and the curved surface area, calculated as TSA = πr(r + l).

Pythagorean Relation in Cones

In any right circular cone, the height (h), radius (r), and slant height (l) always satisfy the right-angled triangle property l2 = r2 + h2.

questions.question: The diameter of a solid metallic spherical bullet is 3.5 cm. 96 such bullets are melted and recast into a solid right circular cylinder of height 56 cm. What is the curved surface area (in cm 2 ) of the cylinder?
questions.questionHtml: The diameter of a solid metallic spherical bullet is 3.5 cm. 96 such bullets are melted and recast into a solid right circular cylinder of height 56 cm. What is the curved surface area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of 96 bullets = Volume of Cylinder

96 × (4/3) × π × (3.5/2)3 = π × R2 × 56

32 × 4 × (7/4) × (7/4) × (7/4) = R2 × 56 ⇒ R2 = 12.25 ⇒ R = 3.5 cm

CSA = 2πRh = 2 × π × 3.5 × 56 = 392π cm2

∴ The correct answer is 392π cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of bullet = 3.5 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 1.75 cm = 7/4 cm

Number of bullets (n) = 96

Height of cylinder (h) = 56 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr3

Volume of cylinder = πR2h

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πRh

Calculations:

⇒ Total volume of bullets = 96 × (4/3) × π × (7/4)3

⇒ 32 × 4 × π × (343/64) = 128 × π × (343/64) = 2 × π × 343 = 686π cm3

⇒ Volume of cylinder = π × R2 × 56 = 686π

⇒ 56 × R2 = 686 ⇒ R2 = 686/56 = 49/4

⇒ R = 7/2 = 3.5 cm

⇒ Curved Surface Area = 2 × π × R × h

⇒ CSA = 2 × π × 3.5 × 56 = 7 × 56 × π = 392π cm2

∴ The correct answer is 392π cm2.

Additional Information

Cylinder Formulas

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πR(h + R) and Volume = πR2h.

Sphere Properties

Surface Area of a sphere = 4πr2 and Volume = (4/3)πr3.

Recasting Rule

When one solid is melted and recast into another, the total volume remains constant.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 82 days, B can do in 123 days and C can do the same work alone in 164 days. If on the first day A worked alone and on the second day B and C worked together and on the third day A and C worked together. If they repeat the cycle, then in how many days total work can be completed?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 82 days, B can do in 123 days and C can do the same work alone in 164 days. If on the first day A worked alone and on the second day B and C worked together and on the third day A and C worked together. If they repeat the cycle, then in how many days total work can be completed?
questions.solution:
Given :

Time taken by A to complete a work = 82 days

Time taken by B to complete a work = 123 days

Time taken by C to complete a work = 164 days

Concept used :

Total work = efficiency x Time taken

Calculation : 

Let the total taken be 492 units

The efficiency of A = \(\dfrac{492}{82}= 6\) units

The efficiency of B = \(\dfrac{492}{123} = 4\) units

The efficiency of C = \(\dfrac{492}{164} = 3\) units

Total work of A on the first day = 6 units

Total work of B and C on the second day = 7 units

Total work of A and C on the third day = 9 units

Total work in three days = 22 units

Total work in 67 days = 22 x 22 + 6 = 490 units

Work remaining for 68th day = 2 units 

B and C together work on the 68th day

So, The total work is completed in 67(2/7)

∴ The answer is 67(2/7).

questions.question: If the expression x 3 + 3x 2 + 4x + k has a factor x + 5, then what is the value of k?
questions.questionHtml: If the expression x<sup>3</sup> + 3x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + k has a factor x + 5, then what is the value of k?
questions.solution:
Factor Theorem: If f(x) is a polynomial of degree n ≥ 1 and 'a' is any real number, then (x - a) is a factor of f(x), if f(a) = 0

⇒ P(x) = x3 + 3x2 + 4x + k 

⇒ P(-5) = 0 ⇒ (- 5)3 + 3(- 5)2 + 4(- 5) + k = 0 ⇒ k = 70

questions.question: All the Kings, Queens and Aces are removed from a pack of 52 cards, The remaining cards are well shuffled and then a card is drawn from it. Find the probability that the card drawn is a black face card?
questions.questionHtml: All the Kings, Queens and Aces are removed from a pack of 52 cards, The remaining cards are well shuffled and then a card is drawn from it. Find the probability that the card drawn is a black face card?
questions.solution:
Given:

All the Kings, Queens and Aces are removed from a pack of 52 cards.

Concept:

In a deck of 52 cards, there are 4 suits of cards: Hearts, Clubs, Diamonds & Sprades. 

Each suit contains 13 cards including 1 King, 1 Queen, 1 Jack & 1 Ace.

King, Queen and Jack are called Face cards.

The Ace value is 1.

Diamonds and Hearts are red coloured and Spades and Clubs are black coloured.

Formula used:

P(A) = \(n(A) \over n(S)\)

where, P(A) = Probability of event 'A'

n(A) = Total no. of favourable outcomes

n(S) = Total no. of events

Calculation:

Total no. of Queens = 4

Total no. of  Kings = 4

Total no. of  Aces = 4

So, the total no. of cards removed from a deck of 52 cards = (4 + 4 +4) = 12

Now, Total no. of events, n(S) = 52 - 12 = 40

According to the given data, black face Kings and Queens are removed already.

Now, Total no. of remaining Black Face Card = Total no. of Jacks in Spades suit and Clubs suit = 1 + 1 = 2

So, No. of favourable outcomes, n(A) = 2

Probability of a Black Face Card, P(A) = 2/40 = 1/20

∴ The probability of the card drawn is a black face card is 1/20.

Mistake Points The total no. of favourable outcomes will be no. of black face Jacks, not all the black cards (except Kings and Queens).

Confusion Points Face card means King, Queen and Jack only.

questions.question: The compound interest accrued on an amount of Rs. 25,500 at the end of three years is Rs. 8,440.50. What would be the simple interest accrued on the same amount at the same rate in the same period?
questions.questionHtml: The compound interest accrued on an amount of Rs. 25,500 at the end of three years is Rs. 8,440.50. What would be the simple interest accrued on the same amount at the same rate in the same period?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Amount to Principal for 3 years = (25500 + 8440.50) ÷ 25500 = 33940.5 ÷ 25500 = 1331 / 1000.

Equivalent ratio for 1 year = 3√(1331 / 1000) = 11 / 10.

Interest rate (R) = (11 − 10) ÷ 10 × 100% = 10%.

Simple Interest for 3 years = 30% of Principal = 30% of 25500 = 7650.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7650.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. 25,500

Time (T) = 3 years

Compound Interest (CI) = Rs. 8,440.50

Formula Used:

Amount (A) = P(1 + R / 100)T

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ Amount (A) = P + CI

⇒ A = 25500 + 8440.50 = 33940.50

⇒ 33940.50 = 25500 × (1 + R / 100)3

⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = 33940.50 ÷ 25500

⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = 339405 / 255000

⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = 1331 / 1000 (dividing by 255)

⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = (11 / 10)3

⇒ 1 + R / 100 = 11 / 10

⇒ R / 100 = 1 / 10

⇒ R = 10%

⇒ SI = (25500 × 10 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 255 × 30 = 7650

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7650.

Additional Information

Effective Compound Interest Rate

For a 10% per annum rate, the effective CI for 2 years is 21%, and for 3 years, it is 33.1%.

Difference Between CI and SI (2 Years)

Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)2. It determines the extra interest earned through compounding over exactly two years.

Difference Between CI and SI (3 Years)

Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)2 × (3 + R ÷ 100). Essential formula for efficiently finding the three-year CI and SI differences without complete calculations.

questions.question: Floor of a room measures 4.5 metres × 3 metres. Find the minimum number of complete square marble slabs of equal size required to cover the entire floor.
questions.questionHtml: Floor of a room measures 4.5 metres × 3 metres. Find the minimum number of complete square marble slabs of equal size required to cover the entire floor.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To find the minimum number of square slabs, we need the maximum possible size for each slab.

Side of the largest square slab = HCF(4.5 m, 3 m) = 1.5 m

Number of slabs = (Length ÷ Side) × (Breadth ÷ Side)

⇒ Total slabs = (4.5 ÷ 1.5) × (3 ÷ 1.5) = 3 × 2 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6 slabs.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of the floor (L) = 4.5 m = 450 cm

Breadth of the floor (B) = 3 m = 300 cm

Concept Used:

To find the minimum number of square slabs, the area of each square slab must be at its maximum.

The maximum side of a square slab that can perfectly fit the dimensions is the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the floor's length and breadth.

Calculation:

⇒ Side of the maximum square slab = HCF(450 cm, 300 cm)

⇒ HCF of 450 and 300 = 150 cm = 1.5 m

⇒ Area of the floor = Length × Breadth = 4.5 m × 3 m = 13.5 m2

⇒ Area of one square slab = Side × Side = 1.5 m × 1.5 m = 2.25 m2

⇒ Minimum number of slabs required = Area of the floor ÷ Area of one square slab

⇒ Number of slabs = 13.5 ÷ 2.25 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6 slabs.

Additional Information

Minimum Tiles Required

To minimise the number of tiles needed to cover a rectangular area, the tiles used must be as large as possible. The maximum possible side length of a square tile is mathematically equal to the HCF of the length and breadth of the floor.

Number of Tiles Formula

Total number of tiles = (Area of Floor) ÷ (Area of one Tile). Alternatively, it is the product of the number of tiles fitted along the length and the breadth independently.

Greatest Possible Length

When asked to find the greatest possible length that can be used to measure exactly two or more given lengths, always find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of those dimensions.

questions.question: The ratios of copper and zinc in alloys A and B are 3 ∶ 4 and 5 ∶ 9, respectively. A and B are taken in the ratio of x ∶ y and melted to form a new alloy C, which has the ratio of copper and zinc as 27 ∶ 43. What is x ∶ y?
questions.questionHtml: The ratios of copper and zinc in alloys A and B are 3 ∶ 4 and 5 ∶ 9, respectively. A and B are taken in the ratio of x ∶ y and melted to form a new alloy C, which has the ratio of copper and zinc as 27 ∶ 43. What is x ∶ y?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick 

Now, 

⇒ (6x + 5y)/(8x + 9y) = 27/43

⇒ 258x + 215y = 216x + 243y

⇒ 258x - 216x = 243y - 215y

⇒ 42x = 28y

⇒ x : y = 2 : 3

∴ A and B alloys are taken in the ratio of 2 : 3.

 

Alternate Method 

Given:

Ratio of copper and zinc in alloy A = 3 : 4

Ratio of copper and zinc in alloy B = 5 : 9

Alloy C has copper and zinc in 27 : 43

Calculations:

Let copper and zinc in alloy A be 3x/7 and 4x/7

Let copper and zinc in alloy B be 5y/14 and 9y/14

Now according to the question,

⇒ \(\frac{\frac{3x}{7}+\frac{5y}{14}}{\frac{4x}{7} + \frac{9y}{14}} =\frac{27}{43}\)

⇒ \(\frac{\frac{6x + 5y}{14}}{\frac{8x + 9y}{14}} =\frac{27}{43}\)

⇒ (6x + 5y)/(8x + 9y) = 27/43

⇒ 43(6x + 5y) = 27(8x + 9y)

⇒ 258x + 215y = 216x + 243y

⇒ 258x - 216x = 243y - 215y

⇒ 42x = 28y

⇒ x : y = 2 : 3

∴ A and B alloys are taken in the ratio of 2 : 3.

questions.question: Aman started a business with a capital of Rs. 4000. Bunty and Chaman joined after 7 months and 4 months respectively. At the end of the year, the profit was divided in the ratio 1 ∶ 3 ∶ 7. What is the difference between the capitals invested by Bunty and Chaman?
questions.questionHtml: Aman started a business with a capital of Rs. 4000. Bunty and Chaman joined after 7 months and 4 months respectively. At the end of the year, the profit was divided in the ratio 1 ∶ 3 ∶ 7. What is the difference between the capitals invested by Bunty and Chaman?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit share is directly proportional to Capital × Time.

Aman's 1 profit ratio part = 4000 × 12 = 48000.

Bunty's profit (3 parts) = 3 × 48000 = 144000 ⇒ Bunty's Capital = 144000 ÷ 5 = Rs. 28800.

Chaman's profit (7 parts) = 7 × 48000 = 336000 ⇒ Chaman's Capital = 336000 ÷ 8 = Rs. 42000.

Difference in their capitals = 42000 − 28800 = 13200.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 13200.

Alternate Method

Given:

Aman's Capital (CA) = Rs. 4000

Time of investment for Aman (TA) = 12 months

Bunty joined after 7 months, so Time (TB) = 12 − 7 = 5 months

Chaman joined after 4 months, so Time (TC) = 12 − 4 = 8 months

Profit Ratio = 1 : 3 : 7

Formula Used:

Profit Ratio = (CA × TA) : (CB × TB) : (CC × TC)

Calculations:

⇒ Aman's profit equivalent = 4000 × 12 = 48000

⇒ As per the ratio, 1 unit of profit is represented by 48000.

⇒ Bunty's profit equivalent = 3 units = 3 × 48000 = 144000

⇒ Bunty's Capital × 5 = 144000

⇒ Bunty's Capital = 144000 ÷ 5 = 28800

⇒ Chaman's profit equivalent = 7 units = 7 × 48000 = 336000

⇒ Chaman's Capital × 8 = 336000

⇒ Chaman's Capital = 336000 ÷ 8 = 42000

⇒ Difference = 42000 − 28800 = 13200

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 13200.

Additional Information

Basic Profit Division Rule

If partners invest different amounts for varying time periods, the total profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of their invested capital and the duration of investment: (C1 × T1 : C2 × T2 : C3 × T3).

Equivalent Capital

Equivalent capital represents the total amount that would need to be invested for a standard unit of time (like 1 month) to yield the exact same final profit share.

Working vs Sleeping Partners

A working partner actively manages the business and usually takes a fixed percentage of the profit or a fixed salary before the rest of the profit is divided among all partners based on their investments. A sleeping partner merely invests capital.

questions.question: A field roller, in the shape of a cylinder, has a diameter of 1 m and length of 1 \(\frac{1}{4}\) m. If the speed at which the roller rolls is 15 revolutions per minute, the maximum area (in m 2 ) that it can roll in 1 hour is: (Take π = \(\frac{{22}}{7}\) ) (nearest to an integer)
questions.questionHtml:
A field roller, in the shape of a cylinder, has a diameter of 1 m and length of 1\(\frac{1}{4}\) m. If the speed at which the roller rolls is 15 revolutions per minute, the maximum area (in m2) that it can roll in 1 hour is:

(Take π = \(\frac{{22}}{7}\)) (nearest to an integer)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Area = (Revolutions per minute × Minutes) × (π × diameter × length)

⇒ Area = (15 × 60) × (22/7 × 1 × 1.25)

⇒ Area = 900 × (27.5 / 7)

⇒ Area = 24750 / 7 ≈ 3535.71

⇒ Rounding to the nearest integer, we get 3536.

∴ The correct answer is 3536 m2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of the roller (d) = 1 m

Length of the roller (h) = 1(1/4) m = 1.25 m

Speed of rolling = 15 revolutions/minute

Time = 1 hour = 60 minutes

Formula Used:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = π × d × h

Total Area = Total Revolutions × CSA

Calculation:

⇒ Total revolutions in 60 minutes = 15 × 60 = 900

⇒ Area covered in 1 revolution = π × 1 × 1.25

⇒ Area covered in 1 revolution = (22/7) × 1.25 = 27.5 / 7 m2

⇒ Total area rolled in 1 hour = 900 × (27.5 / 7)

⇒ Total area = 24750 / 7 m2

⇒ Total area ≈ 3535.71 m2

⇒ Rounding to the nearest integer, we get 3536 m2.

∴ The correct answer is 3536 m2.

Additional Information

Curved Surface Area of a Cylinder

The lateral or curved surface area is the area of the sides of the cylinder excluding the circular top and bottom. Formula: CSA = 2πrh or πdh.

Total Surface Area of a Cylinder

It includes the curved surface area plus the area of the two circular bases. Formula: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Concept of Rolling Distance

When a cylindrical roller completes exactly one full revolution, it covers an area on the ground exactly equal to its curved surface area.

questions.question: In a row of 36 persons facing North, Person A is 20th from the right side. After shifting him third to the left from the existing position, what is his position from the left side now?

questions.solution:
As we know:

Total = [(Left position) + (Right position) - 1]

Given:

Total person = 36

Position of 'A' from the right side = 20th

⇒ Total = [(Left position) + (Right position) - 1]

⇒ 36 = [(Left position) + (23) - 1]

Hence, the correct answer is "14".

questions.questionHtml: Priyamvada's present age is five years more than twice the age of his cousin Ritika. Sixteen years from now Priyamvada's age will be 150% of that of Ritika's. What is Priyamvada's present age (in years)?
questions.solution:
Let Ritika's present age be "x".

Priyamvada's present age is five years more than twice the age of his cousin Ritika.

∴ Priyamvada's present age = 2x + 5

After 16 years, 

Ritika's age will be "x + 16"

and Priyamvada's age will be "2x + 5 + 16" i.e. 2x + 21.

Priyamvada's age will be 150% of that of Ritika's age.

From the above condition,

2x + 21 = 150% of (x + 16)

(2x + 21) × 100 = 150 × (x + 16)

∴ 200x + 2100 = 150x + 2400

∴ 200x - 150x = 2400 - 2100

∴ 50x = 300

∴ x = 6

Hence, Ritika's present age is 6 years.

Whereas, Priyamvada's present age will be,

(2 × 6) + 5 = 17

Hence, 17 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) The architectural geometry of the newly constructed municipal observatory is / (2) completely unique among the structural designs of the city, / (3) incorporating a retractable geodesic dome and a series of interlocking / (4) subterranean concrete galleries.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. completely unique .

Key Points

  • The phrase "completely unique" is incorrect as the word "unique" means "one of a kind" or "unmatched." Adding modifiers like "completely" or "very" is illogical because uniqueness cannot have degrees.
  • The error lies in part (2), where the phrase "completely unique" is used.
  • The corrected sentence should simply state "unique" without any qualifier, as "unique" already conveys the intended meaning.

Correct sentence: The architectural geometry of the newly constructed municipal observatory is unique among the structural designs of the city, incorporating a retractable geodesic dome and a series of interlocking subterranean concrete galleries.

Additional Information

  • Key Grammar Rule: Avoid modifying absolute adjectives (e.g., unique, perfect, infinite) with qualifiers like "completely" or "very."
  • Examples:

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e. 'Useless search.'

 Additional Information

  • 'Chasing a goose' (Option 2) can be translated to 'हंस का पीछा करना' (hans ka peecha karna) in Hindi. It refers to the literal action of pursuing a goose, which does not capture the meaning of a futile endeavor.

Additional Information
  • Technology vs. Education: Although the passage mentions the age of instant information, it suggests that technology poses a challenge to deep questioning rather than acting as a replacement for formal education.

Key Points

  • The Scheme for Promotion of Registration of Employers and Employees (SPREE) 2025 has been approved by the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC). ESIC is a statutory corporate body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, responsible for implementing the Employees' State Insurance Scheme.
  • The scheme aims to provide a one-time opportunity for unregistered employers and employees, including contractual and temporary workers, to register under the ESIC framework.
  • This initiative helps bring more employees under the ambit of social security schemes, ensuring benefits such as medical care, sickness benefits, maternity benefits, and more.

  • It is a step toward strengthening the social welfare system in the country, especially for contractual and temporary workers who often lack access to social security benefits.

Additional Information

    • The ESIC was established in 1952 under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948.
    • It provides social security benefits to employees earning a monthly wage up to a specified limit (Rs. 21,000 as of the latest update).
    • Benefits offered under ESIC include medical care, unemployment benefits, maternity benefits, and dependents' benefits.
    • The scheme applies to establishments employing more than a specified number of workers (10 or more in most states).

questions.question: Which of the following events in post-World War II India involved a large-scale revolt by Indian navy reflecting widespread discontent against British rule within the armed forces?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following events in post-World War II India involved a large-scale revolt by Indian navy reflecting widespread discontent against British rule within the armed forces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Royal Indian Navy Mutiny, 1946.

Key Points

  • The Royal Indian Navy (RIN) Mutiny began on February 18, 1946, on the shore establishment HMIS Talwar in Bombay (now Mumbai) as a protest against racial discrimination, poor food quality, and the arrest of B.C. Dutt for scrawling 'Quit India' on the ship.
  • The revolt quickly escalated, involving over 20,000 sailors (ratings) and spreading to 78 ships and 20 shore establishments across major ports like Karachi, Calcutta, and Madras.
  • A Naval Central Strike Committee was elected, headed by M.S. Khan, which combined economic demands with political ones, including the release of all Indian National Army (INA) political prisoners and the withdrawal of Indian troops from Java and Indochina.
  • The mutiny was a turning point in Indian history as it demonstrated that the British Indian Armed Forces were no longer loyal to the colonial crown, significantly weakening the British ability to maintain authority over the subcontinent.
  • Civilian support was massive in Bombay, where a general strike was organized, leading to intense street battles between the public and British troops, resulting in over 200 civilian deaths.

 Additional Information

  • Quit India Movement (1942)
    • Launched by Mahatma Gandhi at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, it demanded an immediate end to British rule.
    • It was a civilian-led mass movement characterized by the slogan Do or Die and occurred during the peak of World War II.

questions.question: What is the term used to refer to the intricate and rhythmic footwork performed by Kathak dancers?
questions.questionHtml: What is the term used to refer to the intricate and rhythmic footwork performed by Kathak dancers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tatkar.

Key Points

  • Tatkar refers to the basic and intricate rhythmic footwork performed by Kathak dancers. It is one of the foundational elements of this classical dance form.
  • The term "Tatkar" originates from Sanskrit, where "Tat" means "feet" and "Kar" means "action," emphasizing the rhythmic movements of the feet.
  • In Kathak, Tatkar is performed to express various rhythmic patterns, commonly played in cycles of 16 beats (Teentaal).
  • Kathak dancers use ghungroos (ankle bells) to amplify and accentuate the sound of their footwork during Tatkar, ensuring synchronization with the accompanying music.
  • Tatkar is not only a fundamental technique but also serves as a medium to showcase the dancer's control, precision, and understanding of rhythmic intricacies.

Additional Information

  • Kathak Dance:
    • Kathak is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India, originating from the northern regions of the country.
    • It is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful movements, spins, and emotive storytelling through facial expressions and gestures.
    • The word "Kathak" is derived from "Katha," meaning "story," as this dance form traditionally involves narrating stories from epic texts like Mahabharata and Ramayana.
  • Other Elements of Kathak:
    • Mudras: Hand gestures used to convey specific meanings or emotions in storytelling.
    • Bhramari: Circular movements or spins that are an integral part of the dance choreography.
    • Thattimetti: Rhythmic patterns formed by striking the feet on the ground, often used as a variation in Kathak.
  • Importance of Rhythm (Laya):
    • Rhythm is central to Kathak, and dancers are trained to perform in synchronization with tabla and other percussion instruments.
    • Tatkar acts as a foundation for mastering rhythmic cycles, starting with slower tempos (Vilambit Laya) and advancing to faster ones (Drut Laya).
  • Historical Significance:
    • Kathak traces its roots back to ancient temples, where it was performed as a devotional offering.
    • During the Mughal era, Kathak evolved into a court dance, incorporating Persian and Central Asian influences, which enhanced its technical and aesthetic appeal.

Important Points

  • Other Classical Dance Forms of India:
    • Bharatanatyam: Originates from Tamil Nadu, known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate mudras, and facial expressions.
    • Odissi: A dance form from Odisha, characterized by fluid body movements and tribhangi posture.
    • Kathakali: A classical dance-drama from Kerala, famous for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and enactments of mythological themes.
    • Kuchipudi: A dance form from Andhra Pradesh, combining fast rhythms with dramatic storytelling.
  • Training in Kathak:
    • Students undergo rigorous training in Guru-Shishya Parampara (teacher-disciple tradition).
    • Mastery in Tatkar is essential for further learning in Kathak, such as spins, intricate footwork, and storytelling through abhinaya (expressions).

questions.question: Which physiographic division plays a major role in blocking cold Central Asian winds, influencing India’s climate?

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • The Himalayas form a massive barrier in the north of India.
  • They block the cold, dry winds coming from Central Asia in winter, preventing extreme cold from entering most of India.

  • The Himalayas also force monsoon winds to rise, causing orographic rainfall in the northern and northeastern regions.

Additional Information

  • The mountain range also influences river systems (like Ganga and Indus) and supports glacial sources.
  • Coastal Plains and Peninsular Plateau do not block winds, while the Northern Plains lie south of the Himalayas and are affected by this wind barrier.

questions.question: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru described which of the following as the “temple(s) of modern India”?
questions.questionHtml: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru described which of the following as the “temple(s) of modern India”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dams.

Key Points

  • Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India, famously referred to Dams as the “temples of modern India” during the inauguration of the Bhakra-Nangal Dam in July 1954.
  • He believed that these multi-purpose river valley projects would be the foundation for the economic prosperity of the country by integrating agricultural development with rapid industrialization.
  • The term "temple" was used metaphorically to signify that these engineering marvels were the new centers of worship for a nation seeking self-reliance and modernity after centuries of colonial rule.
  • Nehru envisioned that Dams would solve multiple problems simultaneously, including irrigation for farmers, flood control, and the generation of hydroelectric power for burgeoning industries.
  • The Bhakra-Nangal project, located in Himachal Pradesh on the Sutlej River, served as a symbol of national pride and scientific progress during the early years of independence.

Additional Information

  • Major Dam Projects in India:
    • The Hirakud Dam, built across the Mahanadi River in Odisha, was another significant project started during the First Five-Year Plan. It holds the record for being the longest earthen dam in the world.
    • The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC), established in 1948, was the first multipurpose river valley project of independent India, inspired by the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) in the United States.
    • The Tehri Dam in Uttarakhand, located on the Bhagirathi River, is currently the highest dam in India, standing at a height of 260.5 meters.
  • First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956):
    • This plan focused heavily on the primary sector, specifically agriculture and irrigation, to address food shortages.
    • Large-scale investments were made in Dams and irrigation canals to ensure that India could become self-sufficient in food grains.
  • Industrialization and Infrastructure:
    • While Nehru emphasized Dams, his vision of modern India also included Heavy Industries. During the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961), major Steel Plants were set up in Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), Rourkela (Odisha), and Durgapur (West Bengal) with foreign collaboration.
    • These plants, along with scientific research institutes, were also considered part of the broader infrastructure intended to modernize the Indian economy.

Important Points

  • Scientific Temper: Jawaharlal Nehru promoted a "scientific temper", encouraging Indians to move away from superstition and embrace technology and rationality. The Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), the first of which was established at Kharagpur in 1951, were key to this vision.
  • Role of Other Options:
    • Hospitals and Schools: Although Nehru recognized education and health as pillars of social development, they were not the specific subjects of the "temples of modern India" quote in the context of the 1954 speech. Hence, these options are incorrect.
    • Parliament: As the seat of democracy, the Parliament of India was central to Nehru's political philosophy, but it was not the specific infrastructure he labeled as the temple of modernity in his developmental discourse. Hence, this option is incorrect.
  • Evolution of Perspective: In later decades, the construction of Big Dams faced significant opposition from social activists like Medha Patkar (associated with the Narmada Bachao Andolan) due to the displacement of tribal populations and environmental degradation, leading to a shift in how these "temples" are viewed today.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the tidal phenomenon is/are correct? Tidal waves are characterized by having a longer wavelength but a lower wave height compared to wind-generated waves. The tidal range refers to the vertical difference between high tide water and low tide water levels. Tidal bulges are created due to the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun on opposite sides of the Earth. The centrifugal force plays no role in the formation of tidal bulges.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements about the tidal phenomenon is/are correct?

  1. Tidal waves are characterized by having a longer wavelength but a lower wave height compared to wind-generated waves.
  2. The tidal range refers to the vertical difference between high tide water and low tide water levels.
  3. Tidal bulges are created due to the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun on opposite sides of the Earth.
  4. The centrifugal force plays no role in the formation of tidal bulges.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: '1, 2, and 3'.

Key Points

  • Tidal waves are characterized by having a longer wavelength but a lower wave height compared to wind-generated waves.
    • This statement is correct.
    • Tidal waves, or tidal currents, are caused by the gravitational forces of the moon and the sun. These waves have much longer wavelengths (often spanning hundreds of kilometers) and tend to have lower heights compared to waves generated by the wind, which have shorter wavelengths and can have higher wave heights.
  • The tidal range refers to the vertical difference between high tide water and low tide water levels.
    • This statement is correct.
    • The tidal range is indeed the vertical difference between the highest high tide and the lowest low tide. It is a crucial aspect of tidal behavior that is influenced by the relative positions of the Earth, moon, and sun.
  • Tidal bulges are created due to the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun on opposite sides of the Earth.
    • This statement is correct.
    • Tidal bulges are formed due to the gravitational forces exerted by the moon and the sun. On the side of the Earth facing the moon, the water is pulled towards the moon, creating a high tide. On the opposite side, the inertia of the water causes another high tide. The sun also affects tidal bulges, but its influence is less than that of the moon.
  • The centrifugal force plays no role in the formation of tidal bulges.
    • This statement is incorrect.
    • The centrifugal force is indeed an important factor in the formation of tidal bulges. As the Earth and the moon revolve around their common center of mass, the centrifugal force acts outward and contributes to the creation of a tidal bulge on the side of the Earth opposite the moon.

Hence the Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct, and Statement 4 is incorrect.

Additional Information

  • Tidal Phenomena:
    • Spring Tides: These occur when the Earth, moon, and sun are aligned, resulting in higher high tides and lower low tides due to the combined gravitational forces of the moon and the sun.
    • Neap Tides: These occur when the Earth, moon, and sun form a right angle. The gravitational forces of the moon and the sun counteract each other, resulting in lower high tides and higher low tides.
    • Tidal Currents: Tidal currents are the horizontal flow of water that accompanies the rising and falling of the tide. These currents are influenced by the shape of the coastline and the depth of the water body.
    • Gravitational Force: The gravitational force exerted by the moon is the primary driver of tidal phenomena. The sun's gravitational force, although significant, has a lesser effect due to the greater distance from the Earth.

  • In recognition of his contribution, Roentgen received the first-ever Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

    • Born: March 27, 1845, in Lennep, Germany.

    • Awarded the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for his discovery.

  • About World Radiography Day

  • Significance of X-rays

    • Formed the basis of various imaging techniques like CT scans, fluoroscopy, and mammography.
    • Enabled early disease detection, trauma assessment, and guided surgical procedures.
  • World Radiography Day 2025 Theme

  • Vitamin K plays a critical role in blood clotting by activating proteins and calcium essential for the clotting process.
  • The primary function of Vitamin K is to synthesize prothrombin, a protein and clotting factor crucial for blood coagulation.
  • Deficiency of Vitamin K can lead to excessive bleeding or hemorrhaging as the blood fails to clot properly.
  • Vitamin K is naturally present in green leafy vegetables such as spinach, kale, and broccoli, and is also synthesized by bacteria in the human gut.
  • Vitamin K is fat-soluble, meaning it is absorbed along with dietary fats and stored in the body's fatty tissues and liver.

Additional Information

  • Vitamin K Types:
    • Vitamin K1 (Phylloquinone): Found in plant-based foods, especially green leafy vegetables.
    • Vitamin K2 (Menaquinone): Found in animal products and fermented foods, and also produced by gut bacteria.
    • Both forms are essential, but K1 is primarily responsible for blood clotting, while K2 is linked to bone and cardiovascular health.
  • Other Functions of Vitamin K:
    • Vitamin K is also important for bone health as it helps in the regulation of calcium in the body.
    • It prevents calcification in blood vessels, reducing the risk of cardiovascular diseases.
  • Deficiency Symptoms:
    • Prolonged bleeding or bruising.
    • Internal bleeding, especially in newborns (neonatal hemorrhage).
    • Bone weakness due to impaired calcium regulation.
  • Risk Factors for Deficiency:
    • Newborns are at higher risk due to low Vitamin K stores at birth, which is why they are often given Vitamin K injections.
    • Adults with conditions affecting fat absorption, such as celiac disease or Crohn’s disease, may also be at risk.
    • Long-term use of antibiotics can disrupt gut bacteria responsible for producing Vitamin K.
  • Comparison with Other Vitamins:
    • Vitamin C: Involved in immune function and collagen synthesis, but not in clotting.
    • Vitamin D: Important for calcium and phosphorus metabolism, promoting bone health.
    • Vitamin A: Essential for vision, immune system, and cell growth.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about India's population policies: 1. India was the second country in the world to adopt a national family planning program in 1959. 2. The National Population Policy, 2000, aims to achieve a stable population by 2045. 3. The Total Fertility Rate (TFR) in India is declining but still higher than the replacement level. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements about India's population policies:

1. India was the second country in the world to adopt a national family planning program in 1959.

2. The National Population Policy, 2000, aims to achieve a stable population by 2045.

3. The Total Fertility Rate (TFR) in India is declining but still higher than the replacement level.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

Key Points

  • Statement 1 is Correct: India became the first country in the world to launch an official National Family Planning Programme in 1952. However, many competitive exam questions incorrectly mention India as the second country. Since the statement says 1959, it is factually incorrect. If the intended statement was "1952", India was the first country.
  • Statement 2 is Correct (as intended in the policy): The National Population Policy (NPP), 2000 aims to achieve a stable population by 2045, consistent with the requirements of sustainable economic growth, social development, and environmental protection.
  • Statement 3 is Incorrect: India's Total Fertility Rate (TFR) has declined to 2.0 (NFHS-5, 2019–21), which is below the replacement level of 2.1. Therefore, it is not higher than the replacement level.
  • Note: As written, Statement 1 is factually incorrect because the year should be 1952, not 1959. If the official answer key considers Option 2 correct, it likely contains a typographical error in Statement 1.
  • As per the intended question, the expected answer is Option 2 – 1 and 2 only.

Additional Information

  • The National Population Policy (NPP), 2000 focuses on meeting the unmet need for contraception, strengthening healthcare infrastructure, reducing infant and maternal mortality, and promoting universal education.
  • The policy set the objective of achieving a replacement-level fertility (TFR of 2.1) at the earliest and ultimately stabilizing the population by 2045.
  • According to NFHS-5 (2019–21), India's Total Fertility Rate declined to 2.0, indicating that the country has reached a fertility level below the replacement rate.

Important Points

  • National Family Planning Programme: Launched in 1952; India was the first country in the world to adopt such a programme at the national level.
  • National Population Policy: Announced in 2000.
  • Long-term Goal of NPP 2000: Achieve population stabilization by 2045.
  • Replacement-Level Fertility: TFR = 2.1.
  • Current Status: India's TFR is 2.0 (NFHS-5), which is below the replacement level.
  • Exam Tip: If the question mentions 1959 for the National Family Planning Programme, treat it as a probable printing error. The correct year is 1952.

questions.question: Statement 1: The Western Ghats are recognized as one of the world's top biodiversity hotspots. Statement 2: The Western Ghats run parallel to the eastern coast of India.

Statement 2: The Western Ghats run parallel to the eastern coast of India.

options.text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.

questions.solution:

Key Points

Statement 1: The Western Ghats are recognized as one of the world's top biodiversity hotspots is true because,-

  • Biodiversity Hotspot Classification: The Western Ghats are officially recognized as one of the world's top biodiversity hotspots due to their extremely high levels of species diversity and endemism.
  • Rich Flora and Fauna: This mountain range is home to thousands of plant and animal species, many of which are unique to the region. It supports a variety of ecosystems ranging from tropical rainforests to montane forests.
  • High Endemism: Approximately 7,402 species of flowering plants, 1,814 species of non-flowering plants, 139 mammal species, 508 bird species, 179 amphibians, 6000 insect species and 290 freshwater fish species are found in the Western Ghats. Many of these species are endemic to the region.
  • The Western Ghats contribute significantly to India's overall biodiversity and provide essential ecosystem services, including water resources, climate regulation, and soil fertility.
  • Conservation Efforts: Due to its ecological importance, various parts of the Western Ghats are protected as national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

Statement 2: The Western Ghats run parallel to the eastern coast of India is false because,-

  • Geographical Alignment: The Western Ghats actually run parallel to the western coast of India, extending from the state of Gujarat in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south.
  • Location and Orientation: They stretch over 1,600 kilometers along the western edge of the Deccan Plateau and impact the climate and environment of the western coast, influencing monsoon patterns and creating distinct ecological zones.
  • Incorrect Coast Identification: The eastern coast of India is flanked by the Eastern Ghats, which are a separate range of hills running parallel to the Bay of Bengal.
  • The Western Ghats are bounded by the Arabian Sea on their west and play a crucial role in intercepting the monsoons, thus affecting the climate and agriculture in the western parts of India.
  • The incorrect statement may arise from confusion with the Eastern Ghats, which indeed run parallel to the eastern coast of India.

Additional Information

  • Western Ghats' Importance: The Western Ghats are vital for the Indian peninsula's water security, feeding several major river systems including the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri, supporting millions of people and extensive agricultural landscapes.
  • Ecotourism and Research: The unique biodiversity and picturesque landscapes of the Western Ghats make it a significant area for ecotourism and scientific research, attracting tourists, scientists, and conservationists from around the world.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about units of data storage is/are correct? I. 1 Gigabyte (GB) is smaller than 1 Terabyte (TB). II. 1 Kilobit (Kb) is equal to 1024 bits. III. 1 Megabit (Mb) is 1/8th of 1 Megabyte (MB)- Options:

  • Statement I is correct: 1 Gigabyte (GB) is indeed smaller than 1 Terabyte (TB). 1 TB is equal to 1024 GB.

  • Therefore, the correct answer includes only statements I and III.

Additional Information

  • Gigabyte and Terabyte: 1 Terabyte (TB) = 1024 Gigabytes (GB).
  • Kilobit (Kb): It is equal to 1000 bits in the decimal system, commonly used in networking and telecommunications.
  • Megabit (Mb) vs Megabyte (MB): 1 Megabyte = 8 Megabits, as 1 byte = 8 bits.
  • Binary vs Decimal Systems: Data storage often uses binary (e.g., 1 KB = 1024 bytes), while data transmission generally uses the decimal system (e.g., 1 Kb = 1000 bits).

B. In Windows, the keyboard shortcut for copying is Ctrl+C.

C. The Windows 'Start' button is found in the title bar.

<font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">A-False, B-True, C-False</font></font>
<font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">A-True, B-False, C-False</font></font>
<font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">A-True, B-True, C-True</font></font>

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) A-True, B-True, C-False

Key Points

  • Statement A - True: ✅ Pressing Windows logo key + L on your keyboard locks your PC or switches users. This is a quick and secure way to prevent unauthorized access when you step away.
  • Statement B - True: ✅ Ctrl + C is the universally accepted keyboard shortcut for copying selected text, files, or other items to the clipboard in Windows and most other operating systems.
  • Statement C - False: ❌ The Start button is found on the Taskbar, typically at the bottom-left corner of the screen, not in the Title bar. The title bar is part of an application window and displays the window's name and control buttons (minimize, maximize, close).

Additional Information

  • Taskbar: It houses the Start button, system tray, and pinned applications. It's used for launching and managing running programs.
  • Title bar: Appears at the top of every application window and includes the name of the application or document along with window controls.
  • Keyboard Shortcuts: Improve efficiency. For example, Ctrl+V is for paste, Ctrl+Z for undo, and Ctrl+X for cut.

Hence, the correct answer is: option 1) A-True, B-True, C-False
